_meta.purpose: 2.0-A2 T4 — thresholds and window definitions for outcome-measurement confounder detection.
_meta.why_external: These are tuning parameters that will be wrong on first guess. Held in config, following the cloud_ops pack pattern, so a value change alters behaviour with no code deploy.
_meta.evidence_convention: Every threshold declares `basis` as one of: 'measured' (derived from a reproducible measurement, cite it), 'operationally_justified' (a defensible default from domain reasoning, not yet measured), or 'provisional' (a first guess, expected to be wrong). Mirrors discovery/signals/ops_calibration.py, which distinguishes quantitatively-derived defaults from operationally-justified ones.
_meta.honesty_note: No value here scales, weights or corrects a delta. Thresholds decide only whether a CAVEAT is attached. A confounder never adjusts and never blocks a measurement.

volume_shift._note: Total volume shift beyond this fraction between the two measurements attaches a caveat. A signal computed over a materially different total volume is not measuring the same thing, even when the rate looks similar.
volume_shift._basis_detail: No outcome data exists yet to calibrate against — 2.0-A2 in production is what will produce it. 0.25 is a first guess chosen to catch a step change without firing on ordinary drift. Expect to revise.
volume_shift._advisory_note: Between advisory and material the caveat is attached at 'advisory' severity: worth showing, not enough to call the comparison weak.

ci_population._note: The resolved entity set behind the signal. A set that quietly grew or shrank between measurements means the two numbers describe different populations.
ci_population._basis_detail: Chosen to tolerate a single service appearing or disappearing in a small estate while catching a wholesale change. Unmeasured.
ci_population._min_population_note: Below this count a fraction is meaningless (one service out of three is a 33% swing), so an absolute-count rule applies instead.

pack_version._note: A pack's version bumps whenever its detector, scorer or corroboration-rule logic changes (repo convention). Movement measured across a version boundary may reflect a threshold edit rather than a real-world change.
pack_version._basis_detail: Not a threshold — any difference is material. Pack versioning exists specifically so governance can separate a data change from a pack-logic change, so a boundary crossing is always worth surfacing.
pack_version._missing_note: A pack that never stamped a version yields null on one or both sides. That is an absence of information, not evidence of a change, so by default it raises an 'unknown' advisory rather than a material caveat.

seasonality._note: Whether the two windows sit in comparable parts of the year. The window definition is configurable because a hardcoded calendar assumption is wrong for a large share of customers — retail, education, public-sector fiscal years and northern/southern hemisphere operations all differ.
seasonality._basis_detail: calendar_month_overlap is the least-assuming default. It makes no claim about fiscal years or peak periods; it only asks whether the windows cover the same months of the year.
_mode_options: calendar_month_overlap — compare the sets of calendar months each window touches
fiscal_quarter — compare fiscal quarters derived from fiscal_year_start_month
declared_periods — compare against explicitly declared seasonal periods
disabled — do not check seasonality (for an operation with no seasonal pattern)
seasonality._fiscal_note: 1 = January. Set to 4 for an April fiscal year, 7 for July, and so on. Only read when mode is fiscal_quarter.
seasonality._declared_periods_note: Optional list of {"label": str, "startMonth": int, "endMonth": int} for an operation with known peak periods. Only read when mode is declared_periods.

severity._note: Severity labels a caveat's weight for display and counting. It never gates whether the measurement reports.
